statement.essentials: A CT or MRI scan is used when the lump may reach the deep part of the gland or when cancer is suspected, to show how far it goes and what it touches.
statement.anatomy: Imaging defines whether a mass is inside the gland or outside it, looks for features of cancer, and checks for spread. For deep-lobe lesions MRI and CT are the modalities of choice. On MRI, a dark signal on T2-weighted pictures and poorly outlined margins point toward malignancy.
statement.clinical: In 84 consecutive patients with parotid tumours who had MRI before surgery (57 benign, 27 malignant), T2 hypointensity, ill-defined margins, diffuse growth, infiltration of subcutaneous tissue and lymph node enlargement were each associated with malignant histology (P between .001 and .048).

numbers.label: Patients with parotid tumours who had MRI before surgery
numbers.population: Consecutive patients with parotid gland tumours at one university hospital (median age 56 years, range 9 to 85); 29 pleomorphic adenomas, 17 Warthin tumours, 27 malignant tumours
numbers.design: Prospectively included, retrospectively analysed single-centre series

limitations: The MRI series is a single centre with a mixed set of tumour types, of which 29 of 84 were pleomorphic adenomas; its P values show association with malignancy, not predictive accuracy for an individual patient. The cross-section drawn in the atlas is the donor's own normal CT, with the tumour added as an outline: it shows where such a scan cuts, not what a tumour looks like on it.
